about_me.1: My name is Eryk Rozdolski and I do what needs to be done. That is, if I believe something should be done and there is no one better suited than me, I feel obliged to see it through.
about_me.2: Since 2017 at Panie Kolego Projekt. I mainly work as a frontend developer. Through my experience and project interests, it's easier for me to navigate UI/UX topics and design-related areas.
about_me.3: I've been fortunate to write commercially in many different languages such as Python, OCaml, and JavaScript, which allowed me to gain a broad paradigm perspective when it comes to my intuition about what clean code should look like. Today I most often write in JS and focus on problems related to broadly understood web development.
about_me.4: I like to spend my free time actively; I played amateur football for a long time. I devote a lot of time to other sports as well, recently more to jump rope and chess. From time to time I try to record my own music, and if that doesn't work out, I listen to others.

contact_text: Do you have an interesting project for me or are you looking for someone to collaborate with? Let me know, I'll get back to you as soon as possible.
Software Development: In 2026, with the dynamic development of AI tools, my design approach consistently relies on time-tested principles of writing clean = stable software. Code is read (maintained) more often than it is written. It's easier to maintain a small amount of code. There should be as few lines of code as possible until readability is lost. I achieve conciseness, stability, and readability most easily within the functional paradigm, with well-typed abstractions and an understanding of the project's business logic.
Branding: I start the visual identity creation process with a comprehensive interview (briefing), which helps me determine the real needs of my client, possible issues, and solutions that will come into play during the final design stage. I feel satisfaction in this field only when both I as the contractor and the client are happy with the result. I've built my portfolio on many diverse projects, from full brand design (starting with naming—the process of creating a brand name), to visual identity, corporate documents, symbols, and even clothing labels. It's important to me that the client understands how crucial it is to carefully and consistently use not only the logo but the entire designed identity (corporate identity) according to the brand book.
Graphic Design: In graphic design, I focus on combining proper information architecture (exposing the most important messages) with aesthetics that, besides offering something visually engaging and hard to ignore, also carries humor, playfulness, and distance. I try to ensure my designs subtly contain a second layer, are unmistakably original, and are based on clean, readable typography. Less is more, or even less is more and more nowadays
Art: I don't claim to be a musician, writer, or painter, but during my work I've managed to complete several interesting projects with results that gave me some satisfaction. Whether it was research-historical work for a small book "Family Histories," graffiti stencils in my hometown, or my own music tracks, in each case I felt the need to pursue these ideas regardless of financial or time costs. Art, for me, is something that has no value
